status.why: Enacted and effective, but enforcement is paused by the Eighth Circuit since 2 Oct 2026; the record keeps In force and explains this in the notes.

summary_claims.claim: Owners of a website, app or other service must not let users nudify an image or video of an identifiable individual
Civil penalty up to USD 500,000 for each unlawful access, download or use

newer_versions: Eighth Circuit order of 2 Oct 2026 pausing enforcement pending xAI's appeal (news reports only; no order stored); AG release of 4 Sep 2026 on ag.state.mn.us not stored

scope.note: Existing scope note kept: the statute does not name AI; it is Minnesota's operative instrument against deepfake nudification tools.

note: Quotes match the Revisor's session law (signed 7 May 2026, effective 1 Aug 2026) and the bill status page. The scope note is sound: the statute does not name AI, which fits the precedent for non-AI-specific laws. Newer development: the search confirms that on 2 Oct 2026 the Eighth Circuit paused enforcement of the law pending xAI's appeal (several news reports; no court order or official release is stored, and the Attorney General's release of 4 Sep 2026 is not stored). The vocabulary has no status for an enjoined law, so In force with the injunction in the notes is defensible; a maintainer may want to decide. A later run should check the appeal.
